title: Compact cosmic-muon imaging: exposure-time, resolution and detector-cost envelope for a product claim
question: What do peer-reviewed cosmic-ray muon radiography/tomography campaigns and detector-characterisation studies establish about the exposure time, spatial resolution, detector mass, cost and portability trade-off for imaging metre-scale structures such as walls, shafts, soil voids and industrial vessels with passive cosmic-muon detectors, and where is the boundary between demonstrated compact detectors and the active or laser-generated muon concepts the repository keeps separate and non-product-ready?
why_now: The retrospective screening backlog promotes muography to structured screening but blocks it behind a falsification gate on measurement time, detector cost and resolution, and explicitly requires splitting passive cosmic-muon from active/laser-muon concepts. Muography still appears in the advanced-products watch list without a bounded performance envelope, so the advanced track cannot reach a go/hold/reject decision.
real_world_anchor: Measured cosmic-ray muon flux and peer-reviewed muon radiography/tomography performance (exposure time versus spatial resolution versus detector area/cost) and detector technologies such as scintillator+SiPM, resistive plate chambers and drift-tube systems.
novelty_reason: No previous topic addresses muography, cosmic-muon detectors or non-destructive imaging performance; the prior standards, battery, RF, enclosure, photophoretic and drip-emitter topics are unrelated.
